extraction.body: I have used Gboard for years without considering what happens to everything I type. That changed after I read my colleague's article about Gboard being a privacy nightmare. Some details made me uneasy, especially when I thought about the sensitive information that passes through a keyboard I use every day. I have tried plenty of other Android keyboards over the years, but I always seem to come back to Gboard . It's familiar and has the features I've grown used to, so I'm not ready to give it up. I decided to take a closer look at its privacy settings and see if there were any changes I was more comfortable making. Most people don't even realize what it can do The biggest issue for me is that Gboard has network access by default. Gboard uses that connection to send usage information back to Google, including which app you are typing in, how long you type, the word length, and the languages you use. My colleague's report points to a paper in which researchers reconstructed the original typed words from the mathematical updates produced during this training process. In other words, while Google isn't uploading a copy of everything I type, the information produced from that typing isn't necessarily as harmless as I had assumed. There's another concern I hadn't really considered: Gboard's usage data can be tied back to a user. The report says the data collected can include an Android ID, which can potentially be linked to your identity through information associated with your Google account. A keyboard sees an enormous amount of sensitive information, and I wasn't comfortable with so much usage data being collected and with my typing being used to improve Google's models by default. That was enough to make me open Gboard's privacy settings and start turning things off. I opened an app where I could type, brought up Gboard, tapped the settings icon , and went to Privacy . Depending on your phone and Gboard version, you can also find these controls through Settings > System > Keyboard > Gboard > Privacy . Here is what I found there, and what I changed. Gboard can collect usage information to help Google improve the keyboard. Since I don't want Gboard to track my usage, I found little advantage in keeping this feature enabled. Google says Gboard can learn from my typing and voice-typing habits to improve recognition and personalization. This feature stores what it learns on the device, and I can delete the learned words and data in Gboard's Privacy settings. I decided I could live without that extra personalization. Gboard already works well enough for me, and I'd rather not have it continually building up a profile of my typing habits to make predictions a little more tailored. Gboard uses federated learning to learn new words. The app learns from your device's activities and sends insights back to Google. It combines this information with data from other users to improve Gboard's typing and speech models. According to Google, the actual text you type or speak isn't sent to Google through federated learning . The feature is enabled by default, and learning takes place when your phone is charging, connected to Wi-Fi, and not being used. I understand why Google wants to improve Gboard for everyone, but I'm not interested in contributing my typing patterns to that process. So I switched it off. If you use Gboard's voice typing, Google offers the option to donate audio snippets to improve speech recognition. Unlike federated learning, these snippets are sent to Google and are stored there. The snippets can be up to 15 seconds long, or up to 25 seconds when they contain silence or unrecognized audio, and they aren't associated with your Google account. Human reviewers may listen to or transcribe some snippets as part of improving the technology. Audio donations are voluntary, so keeping it off doesn't prevent Gboard's dictation from working. It means I'm not volunteering my voice recordings to help train Google's speech technology. Turns out I'd been doing extra work for years for no reason I've tried other keyboards, but I keep coming back to Gboard because it works well for me. If you use Gboard, it's worth opening the privacy settings and seeing what you've agreed to. You might be perfectly happy with the defaults. I wasn't, and a few small changes made me feel better about continuing to use the keyboard I prefer. The best of Android Police, directly in your inbox.

(Sponsor) Investors pondering whether to buy Bitcoin or XRP right now are faced with two substantially different coins, both of which have experienced notable price declines recently—though not to the same extent. As of October 11, 2026, Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) trades around $82,966, about 34% below its all-time high of $126,080. Meanwhile, XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) trades at about $1.39, roughly 62% below its peak of $3.65. These different drop percentages offer two distinct paths for investors. Choosing Bitcoin may mean trusting a more established market that has shown greater resilience. Conversely, choosing XRP could signal a belief that its larger decline leaves more room for recovery. So, which cryptocurrency best suits your investment goals based on your timeline and risk tolerance? Bitcoin has seen a less severe price drop than XRP, making it look like the steadier option. In 2026, Bitcoin is down just 5.3%, while XRP is down 23.9%. In the past month, Bitcoin has gained 7.3%, significantly outpacing XRP's 2.9% gain. One of Bitcoin's strongest advantages is its robust fund market. The U.S. spot exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that hold Bitcoin manage approximately $105.8 billion. In contrast, XRP ETFs are valued at about $1.6 billion, making Bitcoin's fund market about 67 times larger. This size difference affects who can invest in either coin. Many institutional investors, including those with retirement accounts and various managed portfolios, prefer ETFs over investing directly in cryptocurrencies. Therefore, Bitcoin's larger market opens more doors for institutional money to flow in, as many investment guidelines allow for ETF investments but not direct crypto holdings. However, a larger market also means Bitcoin has less potential for rapid price increases. Because it starts from a much larger market value, any percentage gains require significantly more new investment than XRP. XRP's larger price drop could actually work in its favor for investors willing to ride out more volatility. A 62% decline leaves more room for recovery if demand picks up. Additionally, XRP's smaller market size means similar new investment could lead to a larger price increase. XRP investors have three important developments to consider: The legal battle between Ripple and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has been settled, removing uncertainty from the coin's trading landscape. XRP ETFs reported no outflow days in the week leading up to October 9, suggesting investors kept adding money on some days and pulled none out, even as the market dipped. Evernorth , a treasury company that primarily holds crypto, is set to begin trading on Nasdaq on October 12 after a brief delay. The company holds about 473 million XRP, valued at around $657 million, offering stock investors a new way to gain exposure to XRP. Despite these potential advantages, XRP has continued to lose ground relative to Bitcoin, dropping 7% over the past week while Bitcoin fell only 2.4%. XRP's total decline for 2026 is stark at 23.9%, compared to Bitcoin's modest 5.3%. Thus, any argument for an XRP recovery must also address its ongoing struggles against Bitcoin. A significant price drop doesn't always signal a forthcoming recovery. While some investors may see upside potential, a deeper decline can just as easily signal weaker demand. For most investors—especially those looking to hold for one to two years with a moderate risk tolerance—Bitcoin appears to be the more suitable choice. Its smaller decline, solid 2026 performance, and much larger fund market provide better support during market fluctuations, though both cryptocurrencies carry risks. On the other hand, XRP may appeal to investors with a longer time horizon and higher risk tolerance. If you believe that the resolution of the SEC case and the upcoming Evernorth listing could spur demand, XRP might be worth considering. However, XRP investors should be prepared for greater price swings. If XRP outperforms Bitcoin over the next month and continues to see inflows into its ETFs, that could suggest its larger price drop could lead to future gains. Conversely, if XRP continues to lag behind Bitcoin, the declining-price trend may highlight underlying demand weakness, allowing Bitcoin to maintain its leading position. facts.text: Investors who bought Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) at the all-time high during each of its last three completed cycles waited approximately 39 months, then 36 months, and finally 28 months to return to their original investment level.
Currently, the fourth group of top buyers is still waiting.
Bitcoin peaked at $126,080 on October 6, 2025, and as of October 11, 2026, it is trading near $82,966, roughly 12 months later.
Regardless, buyers who kept buying Bitcoin as prices fell lowered their average cost per coin—meaning they paid less per coin on average.
This is a straightforward calculation and doesn't necessarily guide the best purchase strategy.
Currently, this cycle is about 12 months old, and there has been no recovery yet.
Bitcoin is down 34.2% from its peak and requires a 52% gain to regain that high.
The difference in percentages arises because the decline lowered the starting point, making it harder to climb back above the previous high than to fall.
The first completed cycle peaked on November 30, 2013, at around $1,150.
Bitcoin didn't close above that price again until February 23, 2017, about 39 months later.
In 2017, Bitcoin topped out at about $19,800 on December 17, 2017.
Bitcoin first closed above $20,000 again on December 16, 2020, after about 36 months.
For a buyer at the 2025 peak, two critical factors must occur: Bitcoin needs to remain above its June 30 low of $57,717, which keeps this cycle's worst drawdown at 54.2%.
A close below $57,717 would suggest we might be heading toward deeper troughs like those in past cycles, while a sustained hold would support the view of a less severe cycle.
Each recovery has come faster than the last, but we can't assume that the next recovery will follow the same pattern.
Three cycles offer only a limited perspective, and Bitcoin doesn't follow a set rule that guarantees a similar outcome in future cycles.

MegazoneCloud will resell Portal26’s AI governance platform in Korea, targeting shadow AI, sensitive data risks, compliance and AI costs. AI and cloud company MegazoneCloud has signed a strategic reseller agreement with Portal26 to bring the U.S. company’s generative AI governance and security platform to enterprise customers in Korea. Under an agreement signed September 28, MegazoneCloud will resell Portal26’s AI Adoption Management Platform and provide technical support, while the companies develop governance and security offerings tailored to Korean customer environments. The partnership focuses on unauthorized use of generative AI, exposure of sensitive data, governance, and AI-related costs. Portal26’s AI Adoption Management Platform is designed to detect, analyze, and control generative AI activity across internal development environments, web-based AI services used by employees, and unauthorized shadow AI. The platform provides visibility and controls at the network and browser levels, enabling organizations to identify how generative AI is used across their environments. “As generative AI becomes increasingly embedded across business operations, gaining real-time visibility into unauthorized AI usage and managing the risk of sensitive information leakage at the prompt level have emerged as critical new security challenges,” said Doug Yeum, chief executive officer at MegazoneCloud. Yeum said the companies plan to combine Portal26’s AI visibility and data protection technology with MegazoneCloud’s cloud, AI, and security capabilities to help customers establish governance frameworks around generative AI use. extraction.body: The following is the transcript of the interview with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin that aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Oct. 11, 2026.MARGARET BRENNAN: Good morning, and welcome to Face the Nation. We've got a lot of politics ahead, but we want to start with a quick update on the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall Friday night and resulted in the deaths of four people. For that update, we turn to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. What is needed?SECRETARY OF HOMELAND SECURITY MARKWAYNE MULLIN: Well, we were in touch with the- with all the governors that are affected and might be affected by the continuing storm moving across the nation. Cam Hamilton, who is our director of FEMA, we started pre-positioning assets into every state and working closely with their emergency responders. Right now, from the conversation I've had with each governor, they're in good shape. What's interesting about this area is they're- while they may not have been hit with storms real bad the last two years, they work really, really good together. When I was talking to Governor Kemp from, you know, from Georgia, he was talking about his relationship with Ron DeSantis. When we're dealing with the other governors, they were talking about how they're cooperating with sending assets to the areas that are affected without power to get the- the power restored. FEMA is standing by responding with- with life-saving responses. We were, you know, you never can be fully prepared for- for a storm like this, but I can tell you that the coordination from- from the Oval Office with President Trump's leadership to the- to the governors to the county first responders, we're all working very closely together.MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, we hope everyone in that pathway is safe. There have been at least 30 DHS officer-involved shootings under the Trump administration, according to CBS's tally of events here. There was this incident last week in New York City, and the NYPD did release security video that shows a man dressed as a civilian with a gun drawn approaching a car and then punching in the window. I know you have said there were other DHS ICE officers in the area who were put at risk by the driver, but just to clarify events, when are you going to release the body cameras worn by those officers?SEC. MULLIN: Well, Margaret, what you're seeing is a pole cam. What you're not seeing is actual- the audio footage or a different angle where you have multiple officers that are actually approaching this- this individual named Oscar with a long, very long, extensive rap sheet. He's only been in the country for- for three years, and he has a rap sheet of four charges of felony robbery, two charges of felony assault, felony larceny, misdemeanor assault, possession of- of weapons, possession of stolen property, two felony charges of drugless- of dangerous drugs, and strong gang affiliation that- that has direct or indirect knowledge of- of a CBP officer that was shot last year. We had approached him just like any other undercover agency that's out there, from local, state, federal, or- or county that has undercover officers. He decided that he was going to accelerate and try to evade again. We had taken every precaution to try to keep that from happening, and- and unfortunately, this took place. But as far as--(CROSSTALK)MARGARET BRENNAN: You said they were wearing body cameras. MULLIN:--the information being released--MARGARET BRENNAN: When will you release that footage?(END CROSSTALK)SEC. MULLIN: As far- Margaret, as far as the information being released, FBI and HSI is going to do the investigation. When it's completed, we'll release all the information.MARGARET BRENNAN: Okay. There was that five-year-old you just mentioned. Given that rap sheet and how long you'd been monitoring, how come those officers didn't notice that a child was put in that car?SEC. MULLIN: Well, what- our understanding is- is he drove into the neighborhood. He knew the police was looking for him because, like I said, he just evaded a month ago. He's the one that decided to accelerate and- and ram into another vehicle with his five-year-old in the vehicle, and then tried to accelerate towards other police officers. That's- that is that tells you the type of character that Oscar is, and yet somehow the mayor is out there protesting about this, but yet seven days ago, when NYPD officer got stabbed in the same neighborhood by- by criminals that they released, by the way, Oscar had been released multiple times back onto the streets. Not one time did the governor, not one time did the mayor have a press conference or talk about--(CROSSTALK)MARGARET BRENNAN: They did release a statement and visit the officer in the hospital. MULLIN: --how awful it was that these criminals are stabbing NYPD officers. (END CROSSTALK)SEC. MULLIN: That's right.MARGARET BRENNAN: But I think we're all thankful, as I'm sure you are, that that five-year-old was not harmed. MULLIN: -- Absolutely-- MARGARET BRENNAN: -- about this, though. MULLIN: -- It's frustrating, though, Margaret, because this guy should have never been on the streets because we had asked- we had had a detainer on him and asked the New York City to hand him over to us when they had him on in- in their possession, he was on probation.

extraction.body: The following is the transcript of the interview with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin that aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Oct. 11, 2026.MARGARET BRENNAN: Good morning, and welcome to Face the Nation. We've got a lot of politics ahead, but we want to start with a quick update on the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall Friday night and resulted in the deaths of four people. For that update, we turn to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. What is needed?SECRETARY OF HOMELAND SECURITY MARKWAYNE MULLIN: Well, we were in touch with the- with all the governors that are affected and might be affected by the continuing storm moving across the nation. Cam Hamilton, who is our director of FEMA, we started pre-positioning assets into every state and working closely with their emergency responders. Right now, from the conversation I've had with each governor, they're in good shape. What's interesting about this area is they're- while they may not have been hit with storms real bad the last two years, they work really, really good together. When I was talking to Governor Kemp from, you know, from Georgia, he was talking about his relationship with Ron DeSantis. When we're dealing with the other governors, they were talking about how they're cooperating with sending assets to the areas that are affected without power to get the- the power restored. FEMA is standing by responding with- with life-saving responses. We were, you know, you never can be fully prepared for- for a storm like this, but I can tell you that the coordination from- from the Oval Office with President Trump's leadership to the- to the governors to the county first responders, we're all working very closely together.MARGARET BRENNAN: Well, we hope everyone in that pathway is safe. There have been at least 30 DHS officer-involved shootings under the Trump administration, according to CBS's tally of events here. There was this incident last week in New York City, and the NYPD did release security video that shows a man dressed as a civilian with a gun drawn approaching a car and then punching in the window. I know you have said there were other DHS ICE officers in the area who were put at risk by the driver, but just to clarify events, when are you going to release the body cameras worn by those officers?SEC. MULLIN: Well, Margaret, what you're seeing is a pole cam. What you're not seeing is actual- the audio footage or a different angle where you have multiple officers that are actually approaching this- this individual named Oscar with a long, very long, extensive rap sheet. He's only been in the country for- for three years, and he has a rap sheet of four charges of felony robbery, two charges of felony assault, felony larceny, misdemeanor assault, possession of- of weapons, possession of stolen property, two felony charges of drugless- of dangerous drugs, and strong gang affiliation that- that has direct or indirect knowledge of- of a CBP officer that was shot last year. We had approached him just like any other undercover agency that's out there, from local, state, federal, or- or county that has undercover officers. He decided that he was going to accelerate and try to evade again. We had taken every precaution to try to keep that from happening, and- and unfortunately, this took place. But as far as--(CROSSTALK)MARGARET BRENNAN: You said they were wearing body cameras. MULLIN:--the information being released--MARGARET BRENNAN: When will you release that footage?(END CROSSTALK)SEC. MULLIN: As far- Margaret, as far as the information being released, FBI and HSI is going to do the investigation. When it's completed, we'll release all the information.MARGARET BRENNAN: Okay. There was that five-year-old you just mentioned. Given that rap sheet and how long you'd been monitoring, how come those officers didn't notice that a child was put in that car?SEC. MULLIN: Well, what- our understanding is- is he drove into the neighborhood. He knew the police was looking for him because, like I said, he just evaded a month ago. He's the one that decided to accelerate and- and ram into another vehicle with his five-year-old in the vehicle, and then tried to accelerate towards other police officers. That's- that is that tells you the type of character that Oscar is, and yet somehow the mayor is out there protesting about this, but yet seven days ago, when NYPD officer got stabbed in the same neighborhood by- by criminals that they released, by the way, Oscar had been released multiple times back onto the streets. Not one time did the governor, not one time did the mayor have a press conference or talk about--(CROSSTALK)MARGARET BRENNAN: They did release a statement and visit the officer in the hospital. MULLIN: --how awful it was that these criminals are stabbing NYPD officers. (END CROSSTALK)SEC. MULLIN: That's right.MARGARET BRENNAN: But I think we're all thankful, as I'm sure you are, that that five-year-old was not harmed. MULLIN: -- Absolutely-- MARGARET BRENNAN: -- about this, though. MULLIN: -- It's frustrating, though, Margaret, because this guy should have never been on the streets because we had asked- we had had a detainer on him and asked the New York City to hand him over to us when they had him on in- in their possession, he was on probation.

Ordinary investors, not crypto companies or institutional investors, own most of the world's Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC). Individuals hold about 14 million BTC, or approximately two-thirds of the 21 million BTC that will ever exist, according to River's Bitcoin adoption report for 2026. (River was founded in 2019 to "build the Bitcoin bank of the world.") The distribution of the coin's supply has been on my mind for years now. But I've only understood very recently that other people's misconceptions about who holds the most of it represent a significant buying opportunity. Let's walk through the logic here. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » The biggest single holder of Bitcoin is probably its pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, who disappeared in 2011 and whose identity remains unknown. Many believe that the wallet addresses that are thought to constitute Satoshi's untouched stash hold 968,000 coins, or 4.6% of all that can exist. An investigation by Cointelegraph in September 2026 found that the estimates of the hoard's exact size range from just under 900,000 to about 1.2 million BTC. Those coins have never moved, and given Satoshi's potentially permanent absence, most people, including yours truly, assume that they never will, as to move them would cause widespread panic that they might be sold. There are also an estimated 1.6 million coins that are permanently "lost," i.e., inaccessible to their owners. It is with some regret that I report to you that a small quantity of that lost sum was at one point under my control. Regardless, neither that pile nor Satoshi's are likely to re-enter circulation -- I'm certainly never going to find the wallet credentials I was using more than 10 years ago -- which has the effect of shrinking the pool of coins available to everyone else who might want to buy them. Among the businesses that constitute the biggest potential buyers, Strategy has the most, with 848,000 BTC, or about 4% of the total; every other company combined holds about 3.9%. As you can see, even exchange-traded funds (ETFs) as a group held just 7.1% of the supply despite being issued by major asset managers. And governments hold about 2.5% of the supply as of early October 2026 -- perhaps only a smidgen of what they could ultimately want to hold over the coming years. So what does Bitcoin's ownership and distribution indicate? In short, no single player can dictate its price by manipulating the supply, nor can a major holder manipulate the blockchain's policies, as owning coins does not confer any voting power over the underlying software or the direction that its developers choose to take. The groups that are the most likely to want far more Bitcoin than they currently own, namely corporations, funds, and governments, today own only a minority of it. In 2025, individual holders sold a net 696,000 BTC while businesses bought 489,000, funds and ETFs 205,000, and governments 135,000, according to data from River. If that trend continues, River projects those three groups could own about 11.7 million BTC, or 56% of the supply cap, by 2036. To own more, those groups need to buy it from the people who currently hold it by offering a price that the holders find attractive. Given that Bitcoin's supply is mined at a slower and slower rate after each of its halvings, over the long run it is thus quite likely that aspiring buyers will need to bid more and more to secure a portion of the supply. That's why I believe that buying it now will pay off later. If you have the patience to wait for Bitcoin's slow-moving supply constriction to give way to higher prices, which can take years and is not guaranteed to happen, it's worth buying today and holding while the big accumulators compete for what's left. The big players can always choose to sell instead of buy, but in the long run, it's hard to envision what might make them dump Bitcoin and refuse to buy it again when its price is trending upward. The 10 stocks that made the cut are built for long-term growth and could produce monster returns in the coming years. An investigation by Cointelegraph in September 2026 found that the estimates of the hoard's exact size range from just under 900,000 to about 1.2 million BTC. Those coins have never moved, and given Satoshi's potentially permanent absence, most people, including yours truly, assume that they never will, as to move them would cause widespread panic that they might be sold.

There are also an estimated 1.6 million coins that are permanently "lost," i.e., inaccessible to their owners. It is with some regret that I report to you that a small quantity of that lost sum was at one point under my control. Regardless, neither that pile nor Satoshi's are likely to re-enter circulation -- I'm certainly never going to find the wallet credentials I was using more than 10 years ago -- which has the effect of shrinking the pool of coins available to everyone else who might want to buy them.
Among the businesses that constitute the biggest potential buyers, Strategy has the most, with 848,000 BTC, or about 4% of the total; every other company combined holds about 3.9%.

As you can see, even exchange-traded funds (ETFs) as a group held just 7.1% of the supply despite being issued by major asset managers. And governments hold about 2.5% of the supply as of early October 2026 -- perhaps only a smidgen of what they could ultimately want to hold over the coming years.
So what does Bitcoin's ownership and distribution indicate?

In short, no single player can dictate its price by manipulating the supply, nor can a major holder manipulate the blockchain's policies, as owning coins does not confer any voting power over the underlying software or the direction that its developers choose to take.

The groups that are the most likely to want far more Bitcoin than they currently own, namely corporations, funds, and governments, today own only a minority of it. In 2025, individual holders sold a net 696,000 BTC while businesses bought 489,000, funds and ETFs 205,000, and governments 135,000, according to data from River. If that trend continues, River projects those three groups could own about 11.7 million BTC, or 56% of the supply cap, by 2036.

To own more, those groups need to buy it from the people who currently hold it by offering a price that the holders find attractive. Given that Bitcoin's supply is mined at a slower and slower rate after each of its halvings, over the long run it is thus quite likely that aspiring buyers will need to bid more and more to secure a portion of the supply. That's why I believe that buying it now will pay off later.

If you have the patience to wait for Bitcoin's slow-moving supply constriction to give way to higher prices, which can take years and is not guaranteed to happen, it's worth buying today and holding while the big accumulators compete for what's left. The big players can always choose to sell instead of buy, but in the long run, it's hard to envision what might make them dump Bitcoin and refuse to buy it again when its price is trending upward.

Bitcoin ( CRYPTO:BTC ) reaching $1 million and XRP ( CRYPTO:XRP ) hitting $10 are two major price points that many holders frequently discuss when looking ahead to the next cycle for both cryptocurrencies. While $1 million for Bitcoin may sound astronomical and $10 for XRP seems more achievable, the gap between these two targets may not be as wide as it appears.

For perspective, Bitcoin needs to grow 12.1 times from its current price of $82,965 as of October 11, 2026. In contrast, XRP needs to grow only 7.2 times from its current price of $1.39. This means XRP has a shorter distance to climb.

When comparing price targets, it’s essential to understand how far each cryptocurrency must rise to meet those goals. A multiple effectively measures this journey by showing how much each coin must increase in value. For Bitcoin, that’s a significant 12.1x increase; meanwhile, XRP only needs to grow 7.2x . Based on this analysis, XRP has a clearer path to its target.

Looking at historical trends can provide additional context. Between 2016 and 2021, Bitcoin rose 12x. Meanwhile, XRP surged about 7 times between 2024 and 2025, rising from about $0.50 to its 2025 peak.

Each target is roughly comparable to past price surges of each coin, which lends credibility to the potential for achieving these numbers. However, it’s important not to overlook the overall market dynamics required for both cryptocurrencies to reach their targets.

Market capitalization—calculated by multiplying the cryptocurrency’s price by the number of coins in circulation—gives a clearer picture of the asset’s worth and what it takes to reach a specific price target.

As of now, Bitcoin’s market value is around $1.67 trillion with roughly 20.1 million coins in circulation. For Bitcoin to reach $1 million per coin, its total market value would skyrocket to about $20.1 trillion. This figure represents an unprecedented demand for funds in the cryptocurrency market.

On the other hand, XRP has about 63.1 billion coins available. For XRP to reach $10, its market value would be only about $631 billion. Even at that price, XRP would be only about 38% of Bitcoin’s current market value, meaning that XRP at $10 would still be smaller than Bitcoin is now.

When considering both the required multiple and market demand, XRP clearly comes out ahead. It requires a smaller growth multiple and substantially less new investment than Bitcoin, which needs a much larger market influx.

Both coins have to overcome several price levels before reaching their targets. XRP has dropped 41.3% over the past year and must first reclaim the $1.84 mark, where it started 2026. This represents a 32.4% increase from its current price. The next level to beat is $2.38, 71.2% above its current price. Only then would $10 be a serious possibility.

Similarly, Bitcoin must move past certain price thresholds . It started 2026 at $87,498, 5.5% above its current trading price, and was $110,769 a year earlier, 33.5% higher than where it trades now. Both critical price points are still well above Bitcoin’s current price.

Based on the analysis, XRP hitting $10 appears to be the more achievable target of the two. XRP’s required 7.2-fold increase is far less daunting than Bitcoin’s 12.1-fold rise.
